solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Suspect smiled having ensnared a fool (7)

indicators.note: suspect letters are not to be trusted as they stand, so rearrange them
the rearranged letters trap A inside them

blocks.note: A slips in before the final D

annotation.surface: A grinning suspect has caught out some gullible person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun, the person who smiled, but it is an adjective telling you the letters of 'smiled' are dodgy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to fool someone is to lead them astray.

entries.clue: All kicking off with horrendous answer, tricky question (4)

indicators.note: every word only starts, so take just the first letter of each

blocks.note: first letters of With, Horrendous, Answer, Tricky

annotation.surface: Someone gives a horrendous answer to a tricky question and everything kicks off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tricky question' looks like one phrase for the definition, but 'tricky' is the last word of the fodder and 'question' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: WHAT is the basic question word, and an exclamation of disbelief.

entries.clue: Still Creator showed up before Egyptian god (6)

annotation.surface: A religious scene: the Creator appears, ahead of an Egyptian deity.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes 'Creator' look divine and 'Still' look like 'even so'; read together they are a maker of stills, a photograph.
annotation.definitionFit: A camera creates stills, i.e. photographs.

entries.clue: Guiding light, top laser manoeuvred (4,4)

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new position

annotation.surface: A high-end laser being steered as a guiding beam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guiding light' reads as a mentor, and the laser suggests a beam; the answer is the star sailors steered by.
annotation.definitionFit: Polaris, the pole star, has long guided navigators, so it is literally a guiding light.

entries.clue: Youth, a support on trail (10)

blocks.note: the dole is state benefit, financial support
a scent is the trail a hound follows

annotation.surface: A young person being propped up while out on a trail.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the first two chunks sit on top of the third. The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
annotation.definitionFit: A youth is an adolescent, a young person between child and adult.

entries.clue: Cut, gerbil or hamster for example bit (7)

annotation.surface: A pet gerbil or hamster that has been cut, or has bitten someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as the past tense of bite, as if the rodent turned on its owner; it is the noun, a small piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small fragment snipped off something, of text or talk especially.

entries.clue: Home impressing yours truly, the entrance to mine (7)

indicators.note: the home presses in around the other letters, holding them inside

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a home

annotation.surface: Someone's house is impressive enough to be the gateway to their own place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive, 'belonging to me', but it is the coal mine.
annotation.definitionFit: A pithead is the top of a mineshaft, where miners go in.

entries.clue: Excuse prisoner, cheated (7)

blocks.note: done = swindled, as in 'I've been done'

annotation.surface: A prisoner complaining he was cheated, as an excuse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Excuse' reads as a noun, the prisoner's excuse, but it is the verb: to let an offence pass.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to forgive or overlook wrongdoing, usually with a hint of tacit approval.

entries.clue: Simple but effective remedy tricks killer? (5,6)

blocks.note: a bullet kills; the question mark admits it is only one example

annotation.surface: A cure that works by fooling a killer disease.
annotation.walkthrough: A magic bullet was first a drug that strikes only the disease, which the surface's 'killer' echoes.
annotation.definitionFit: A magic bullet is a simple, sure fix for a hard problem.

entries.clue: Nonetheless, nothing different? (3,3,4)

blocks.note: an adverb for 'even so', used to concede a point
read literally: everything identical, with no variation

annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: if nothing differs, everything is all the same.
annotation.definitionFit: 'All the same' means nonetheless, and also means identical throughout.

entries.clue: Run south away from incline (4)

indicators.note: S goes away, leaving the rest of the word

blocks.note: an incline is a slope; its first letter is the one to remove

annotation.walkthrough: 'Run south' reads as a direction of travel, but south is only the letter S, taken off the front of the incline.
annotation.surface: A runner heading south, off the hill.
annotation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy strides.

entries.clue: Dead sheep, one for meat (8)

blocks.note: a ram is a male sheep

annotation.surface: A dead sheep, one of them destined for the table.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all mutton, but pastrami is beef.
annotation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a spiced, smoked cured meat.

entries.clue: Final game, picking up crashing wave in Phuket? (10)

indicators.note: as a microphone picks up sound, go by how it is heard

blocks.note: a breaker is a crashing wave; one at Phuket, in Thailand, is a Thai breaker

annotation.surface: A surfing contest's last round in Thailand.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Phuket is just one Thai example. Thai is said exactly like 'tie'.
annotation.definitionFit: A tiebreaker is the extra final game played to settle a tied score.

entries.clue: Sample spud, little bit of salt in it (6)

indicators.note: only the first small piece of the word, its first letter
'it' is the spud, and the S is put in it

annotation.surface: Try a potato with a pinch of salt on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sample' looks like a verb, as in taste the spud; it is the noun, a trial portion.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small portion offered to try before committing to more.

entries.clue: Cereal grains in paella with berry stirred up (5,6)

indicators.note: stirring mixes the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters; 'with' just joins the two words

annotation.surface: A recipe: grains going into a paella with a berry stirred through.
annotation.walkthrough: Stirring fits the kitchen scene so neatly that it hides as a cooking step.
annotation.definitionFit: Pearl barley is barley grain polished into small round pearls.

entries.clue: Working idler, he’s greatly appreciated! (8)

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An idler who finally gets a job is thanked warmly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greatly appreciated' seems to praise the worker, but it is past tense: enjoyed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to relish is to enjoy keenly, the past tense matching 'appreciated'.

entries.clue: Insincere broadcast entertaining chamber (7)

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest has them inside

blocks.note: to broadcast seed is to sow it, scattering by hand
a hall is a large room

annotation.surface: A hollow programme, with a room full of entertainers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' pulls toward radio and TV, but it is the farming verb; 'entertaining' then means holding the room inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Shallow feeling is insincere, lacking depth.

entries.clue: Erase wound (7)

blocks.note: to strike out, as when a runner is withdrawn from a race
a noun here: a light graze, not the past tense of wind

annotation.walkthrough: 'Wound' could be read as the past tense of wind; it is the injury, a noun beside a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: to delete a name from a list, and a shallow cut on the skin.

entries.clue: Beethoven’s ninth sandwich, or a lot’s consumed! (6)

indicators.note: the answer has been eaten up inside these words

blocks.note: starts in the last two letters of 'sandwich', runs through 'or a', ends in the L of 'lot's'

annotation.surface: A sandwich eaten while listening to Beethoven's Ninth, or plenty of them.
annotation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony is nicknamed the Choral for the Ode to Joy chorus in its last movement; the letters sit in sandwi(CH OR A L)ot.
annotation.definitionFit: The Choral is the name of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

entries.clue: Maybe face decorator‘s insolence and verbal abuse (8)

definitions.note: 'maybe' because lipstick is only one way to decorate a face

blocks.note: giving someone stick is British slang for criticising them

annotation.surface: A painter-decorator is cheeky and insulting on the job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face decorator' suggests a tradesman painting a building's facade; it is make-up for a face.
annotation.definitionFit: Lipstick is cosmetic colour for the lips, decorating the face.

entries.clue: Making shrill sounds, squealer jabbed by nail (6)

indicators.note: the nail is stuck into the squealer

blocks.note: a pin is a small nail

annotation.surface: A pig squealing after being stabbed with a nail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Squealer' looks like an informer; it is the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: Piping is making a high, shrill sound, like a pipe.

entries.clue: Insect a fairy knocked over (4)

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round

blocks.note: an elf is a fairy creature

annotation.surface: A bug that has flattened a fairy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bug toppling a sprite; 'knocked over' only tells you to turn the letters round.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the flea is a wingless, jumping, blood-sucking insect.

entries.clue: Person dropping off helped, easy to go astray (10)

indicators.note: the letters wander out of their places

annotation.surface: Someone making a delivery found it easy to get lost despite help.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' reads as delivering something; it means falling asleep.
annotation.definitionFit: A sleepyhead is a drowsy person, someone nodding off.

entries.clue: Great deal covered in the appraisal (4)

indicators.note: the answer lies under cover inside these words

blocks.note: begins after the T of 'the' and ends two letters into 'appraisal'

annotation.surface: A property bargain, all set out in the valuation report.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great deal' reads as a bargain; here it means a large amount. The letters sit in t(HE AP)praisal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'a heap' or 'heaps' is informal for a large quantity.

entries.clue: Float boarded by the two of us, 10 Across (7)

definitions.note: 10 Across is ALL THE SAME, meaning nonetheless

indicators.note: passengers boarding a vessel go inside it

annotation.surface: A pair of friends climbing aboard a raft.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Float' looks like a noun, a raft being boarded; it is the verb, to hover.
annotation.definitionFit: However means nonetheless, the sense of 10 Across.

entries.clue: Youth I found originally residing in French city (7)

indicators.note: take what 'found' is at its origin, its first letter
a resident lives in a place, so F takes up residence inside the city

blocks.note: first letter of found; it sits after the first N

annotation.surface: In my youth I was first discovered living in a French city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found originally' reads as a biography, being discovered early on, but it only yields F.
annotation.definitionFit: Youth as a stage of life: infancy is the earliest part of it.
